tools.name: managed_agents_create_session
tools.title: Start a Managed Agents session
tools.description: Starts a session of an agent in an environment, optionally with a first message. Pass an idempotencyKey so a retried call never starts a second session. Read the reply with managed_agents_list_events (wait: true). If the agent requires approval for a tool, the turn stops until the user decides: see managed_agents_list_pending_approvals and managed_agents_answer_approval.

message.description: A first user message, queued before the session starts.

idempotencyKey.description: Recommended. A key unique to this session (16-128 letters, digits, - or _). Reuse the same key when you retry the same call: the server answers from the first attempt instead of starting a second session. A new key starts a new session. Without a key, each tool call gets its own, so a call the host retries is not deduplicated.

meta.description: The call's response meta: request id, idempotency key and whether the server replayed an earlier result.

tools.name: managed_agents_send_message
tools.title: Send a message to a Managed Agents session
tools.description: Appends a user message to a session and returns the appended events. Pass an idempotencyKey so a retried call never sends the message twice. Read the reply with managed_agents_list_events (wait: true, after: the returned seq). A session waiting on a tool approval rejects new messages (409 tool_result_required): answer it first with managed_agents_answer_approval.

idempotencyKey.description: Recommended. A key unique to this message (16-128 letters, digits, - or _). Reuse the same key when you retry the same call: the server answers from the first attempt instead of appending it twice. A new key sends a new message. Without a key, each tool call gets its own, so a call the host retries is not deduplicated.

items.description: A session event: the envelope (id, seq, sessionId, createdAt) and a body that depends on type.

meta.description: The call's response meta: request id, idempotency key and whether the server replayed an earlier result.

tools.name: managed_agents_answer_approval
tools.title: Answer a tool approval request
tools.description: Allows or denies one tool call waiting for approval in a Managed Agents session. Only answer as the user decided; never allow on your own judgment. Repeating the same answer (same decision and message) is safe. Errors: 409 tool_result_already_submitted when the request already has an answer (including Ryu's denial at expiresAt), 409 unknown_tool_use when the toolUseId is not pending (a wrong id, or a request an interrupt abandoned). Then read the rest of the turn with managed_agents_list_events (wait: true, after: the returned seq minus 1).

toolUseId.description: The toolUseId (mtool_…) of the open request, from managed_agents_list_pending_approvals.

decision.description: "allow" runs the tool call; "deny" refuses it.

message.description: With deny: why, shown to the model.

data.description: A session event: the envelope (id, seq, sessionId, createdAt) and a body that depends on type.

meta.description: The call's response meta: request id, idempotency key and whether the server replayed an earlier result.

tools.name: managed_agents_list_events
tools.title: List Managed Agents session events
tools.description: Reads a session's event log after a seq. With wait: true, follows the live stream until the turn ends (bounded by maxEvents and timeoutMs) and reports whether it ended. When the turn stopped on a tool approval, the result has requiresAction: true and the pending toolUseIds: the task is not done; call managed_agents_list_pending_approvals and ask the user.

after.description: Only events with a higher seq (default 0).

wait.description: Follow the live stream until the current turn ends instead of reading one page.

maxEvents.description: With wait: stop after this many events (default 100).

timeoutMs.description: With wait: stop waiting after this long (default 60000).

items.description: A session event: the envelope (id, seq, sessionId, createdAt) and a body that depends on type.

data.description: Without wait: one page (data, hasMore, headSeq, nextAfter). With wait: the events followed (data), turnEnded and timedOut, plus requiresAction, pendingToolUseIds and next when the turn stopped on a tool approval.

meta.description: The call's response meta: request id, idempotency key and whether the server replayed an earlier result.

tools.name: messaging_status
tools.title: Check Ryu Messaging status
tools.description: Reports whether the Ryu control plane has Messaging configured and which channels can send (configured, channels.sms, channels.mms, channels.voice, channels.whatsapp, apiVersion). It describes the deployment, not your organization: Ryu enables Messaging per organization and the organization also turns on its Messaging feature, which this does not show. Needs no key, so it works before RYU_API_KEY and RYU_ORGANIZATION_ID are set, and then sends neither.

tools.name: messaging_send_sms

An `outcome_unknown` error means it may have been sent; read the message with messaging_get_message before sending again with a new key.

from.description: The id of one of the organization's numbers with the SMS capability (see messaging_list_numbers).

messageType.description: AWS message type (default TRANSACTIONAL). Use PROMOTIONAL for marketing.

ttlSeconds.description: How long AWS keeps trying to deliver, 5 to 259200 seconds.

metadata.description: Up to 16 entries, returned on the message and its webhooks.

idempotencyKey.description: Required. A key unique to this SMS. Reuse it when you retry the same send: the server replays the first result instead of sending and charging again, unless the first attempt was refused (provider_refused or a 4xx), which frees the key for a new attempt. A new key sends a new SMS.

tools.name: mail_create_inbox
tools.title: Create a Mail inbox
tools.description: Creates an inbox to send and receive email from and returns it with its id and address. `clientId` is required: a retry with the same one gives back the inbox already made. Self-hosted Mail needs `address`; hosted Mail ignores it and builds the address from `localPart`, else from `name`, on its default domain or `domainId`. A hosted key needs the mail:manage scope.

name.description: Display name, also used as the sender name, e.g. 'Support agent'. Hosted Mail derives the address from it when no localPart is given.

clientId.description: Required. Your own id for this inbox (printable ASCII, no leading or trailing space). Creating again with the same clientId gives back the inbox already made instead of a second one, so reuse it when you retry.

address.description: Self-hosted Mail: required, the inbox's full address, e.g. 'support@example.com'. Hosted Mail ignores it.

localPart.description: Hosted Mail: the part before the @. A taken or invalid one is refused rather than changed; omit it to derive one from name. Self-hosted Mail ignores it.

domainId.description: Hosted Mail: a verified custom domain to create the address on; omit for the default domain.

podId.description: The pod (group of inboxes) to put the inbox in.

description.description: Hosted Mail: a note about what the inbox is for. Self-hosted Mail ignores it.

meta.description: The call's response meta: request id, idempotency key and whether the server replayed an earlier result.

tools.name: mail_send
tools.title: Send an email
tools.description: Sends an email from one of your inboxes to real recipients. Name the inbox in `from` (its address or id; the hosted Ryu MCP server's `mail_send` takes `inboxId` and `organizationId` instead). Give exactly one of `text` or `html`. `idempotencyKey` is required: reuse it to retry the same send safely, and use a new one for a new email. With no inbox yet, create one with `mail_create_inbox` (a write tool: an MCP server offers it only when writes are allowed, and a hosted key needs the mail:manage scope); without it, ask the person to create one with the SDK's `mail.inboxes.create` or the CLI's `mail inboxes create`.

from.description: The sending inbox: its address (e.g. 'agent@example.com') or its id from mail_list_inboxes.

bcc.description: Blind-copy recipient addresses, hidden from the other recipients.

subject.description: The subject line, e.g. 'Your build finished'.

text.description: Plain-text body. Give exactly one of text or html.

html.description: HTML body. Give exactly one of text or html.

idempotencyKey.description: Required. A key unique to this email (printable ASCII, 1-255 characters). Reuse the same key when you retry the same send: the server answers from the first attempt instead of sending again. A new key sends a new email.

meta.description: The call's response meta: request id, idempotency key and whether the server replayed an earlier result.

tools.name: notify_publish
tools.title: Publish a Notify event
tools.description: Publishes an event to the Notify inbox; it reaches live streams and the tenant's delivery destinations (webhooks, ntfy). Pass an idempotencyKey so a retry never publishes twice.

topic.description: Stream or topic name that subscribers filter on, e.g. 'deploys'.

recipient.description: Your own label for who the event is for, e.g. 'oncall'. Recipient preferences (mute, quiet hours) apply to it.

tags.description: Labels for filtering, at most 16, e.g. ['release', 'web'].

idempotencyKey.description: Recommended. A key unique to this event (printable ASCII without spaces, 1-128 characters). Reuse the same key when you retry the same call: the server answers from the first attempt instead of publishing a second event. A new key publishes a new event. Without a key, each tool call gets its own, so a call the host retries is not deduplicated.

response.description: The interactive response (approval, yes/no, text), or null.

tools.name: notify_request_approval
tools.title: Ask a person for approval
tools.description: Publishes an approval (or yes/no) request and waits up to waitMs (default 45 s) for someone to answer in Notify. Returns approved, status (approved, denied, yes, no, expired, canceled, or pending) and timedOut. status pending with timedOut false means the request is still open until timeoutMs: poll notify_get_event with event.id instead of calling this tool again, which would publish a second request.

topic.description: Stream or topic name that subscribers filter on, e.g. 'deploys'.

source.description: Label for what produced the event, e.g. 'ci' or 'agent-mail'.

recipient.description: Your own label for who the event is for, e.g. 'oncall'. Recipient preferences (mute, quiet hours) apply to it.

tags.description: Labels for filtering, at most 16, e.g. ['release', 'web'].

prompt.description: The question shown with the event, e.g. 'Ship build 184?'.

responseType.description: approval (approve or deny, the default) or yes_no.

timeoutMs.description: How long the request stays open, in ms (default 600000, at most 900000). Notify expires it at that moment.

waitMs.description: How long this call waits for an answer, in ms (default 45000, at most 50000). If nobody has answered by then, the result is status pending with the event; read it later with notify_get_event.

idempotencyKey.description: Recommended. A key unique to this approval request (printable ASCII without spaces, 1-128 characters). Reusing it never publishes a second request, but it does not replay the first: each call sets a new deadline, so Notify refuses the retry with idempotency_conflict. After a lost reply, poll notify_get_event with the first call's event.id, or find the event with notify_list_events. A new key publishes a new request. Without a key, each tool call gets its own, so a call the host retries publishes a second request.

status.description: approved, denied, yes, no, expired, canceled, or pending (still open).

response.description: The interactive response (approval, yes/no, text), or null.

meta.description: The call's response meta: request id, idempotency key and whether the server replayed an earlier result.

tools.name: box_get
tools.title: Get a Box
tools.description: Returns one Box with its id, name, size, status (provisioning, ready, running, stopped or error), lastError and network policy. Poll it after box_create until the status leaves provisioning.

tools.name: box_create
tools.title: Create a Box
tools.description: Creates a persistent Linux workspace. It is ready at once, or provisioning while setup runs; check its status with box_get before box_exec. Setup commands run as root and, on a Box with egress, can reach the network. Pass an idempotencyKey so a retried call never creates a second Box.

name.description: Box name (default mcp-<12 hex>, derived from idempotencyKey when one is given).

setup.description: Shell commands run as root, in order, before the Box is ready. With setup the Box comes back provisioning.

idempotencyKey.description: Recommended. A key unique to this Box (printable ASCII without spaces, 1-128 characters). Reuse the same key when you retry the same call: the server answers from the first attempt instead of creating a second Box. A new key creates a new Box. Without a key, each tool call gets its own, so a call the host retries is not deduplicated.

meta.description: The call's response meta: request id, idempotency key and whether the server replayed an earlier result.

tools.description: Creates a private Site with a starter template (website, help-center, dashboard, game or reset-calendar) and returns it, with the id and revision sites_deploy takes. Nothing is published until you deploy. A slug already in use is refused with 409 conflict.

tools.name: sites_deploy
tools.title: Deploy a Site
tools.description: Publishes a Site: with html, saves it as a new version and serves it; with versionId, serves a saved version. The version must pass the secret scan (422 security_blocked otherwise). Requires the expectedRevision you read with sites_get. Returns { project, version, url }. Never changes who can visit: a new Site stays private. Ask the user before deploying.

siteId.description: The Site id from sites_list or sites_get, not its slug.

html.description: A complete, self-contained HTML document beginning with <!doctype html> (inline CSS and JS only). Saved as a new version, then deployed. Give html or versionId.

versionId.description: A saved version to deploy instead of new html.

expectedRevision.description: The Site revision you last read from sites_get. Required: read the Site first. A stale revision is refused with 409 conflict; read the Site again before retrying.

version.description: The deployed version; null only when Sites left it out (the deploy still committed).

meta.description: The call's response meta: request id, idempotency key and whether the server replayed an earlier result.

tools.name: sites_update_settings
tools.title: Change who can visit a Site
tools.description: Changes a Site's audience (private, invited, workspace or public), its invited viewers, workspace, optional sign-in or remix opt-in, and keeps every other setting (editors are not changed here). Requires the expectedRevision you read with sites_get; a stale one, including a repeat after a change already applied, is 409 conflict, so read the Site again before retrying. public needs the operator to allow public Sites (403 policy_denied otherwise); invited, workspace and optional sign-in need the process's OpenID Connect sign-in (503 unavailable otherwise, not retryable). Returns the Site with its new revision. Ask the user before widening access, above all before making a Site public.

siteId.description: The Site id from sites_list or sites_get, not its slug.

audience.description: private: only the owner; invited: the viewers list, after signing in; workspace: members of workspaceId; public: anyone with the URL. public works only when the operator allows public Sites (RYU_SITES_PUBLIC=1 or the runtime config's publicEnabled, which the SDK's ryu.sites.status() reports), otherwise 403 policy_denied. invited and workspace need the process's OpenID Connect sign-in (503 unavailable otherwise).

viewers.description: Invited viewer emails for audience invited (at most 100). Replaces the current list.

workspaceId.description: The workspace whose members may visit, for audience workspace; null clears it. You must belong to it (403 forbidden otherwise): a standalone Sites process without Ryu Core gives its management caller no workspaces, so it refuses every workspaceId.

optionalSignIn.description: Offer visitors an optional sign-in. Needs the process's OpenID Connect sign-in (503 unavailable otherwise).

allowRemix.description: Let anyone who may visit start their own private copy of the deployed version.

expectedRevision.description: The Site revision you last read from sites_get. Required: read the Site first. A stale revision, including a repeat of a change that already applied, is refused with 409 conflict; read the Site again before retrying.

meta.description: The call's response meta: request id, idempotency key and whether the server replayed an earlier result.
